fullText:
Summary: Tokyo Cement Company (Lanka) PLC (TKYO.N0000 voting, TKYO.X0000 non-voting) is Sri Lanka's market-leading cement maker. Sales are growing fast (revenue up 27% in the six months to September 2026, volumes up 28% last year), but profit is falling: the industry hasn't raised prices while costs rose, and interest costs went up after the Trincomalee expansion and the new coastal ship. Return on equity has been only about 8% for two years and about 9% on average over five years, well below the roughly 15.5% a Sri Lankan shareholder should expect. At Rs 84.70 the voting share is 1.17x its NAV of Rs 72.51 and 15.5x trailing earnings. The methods put fair value at about Rs 45, so the price is about 88% above it. I'd buy at up to about Rs 38.30 and treat under Rs 33.80 as a strong buy. The non-voting share (about Rs 63.50) gets the same dividend and is about 25% cheaper, so it is the better class if you buy, but it is also above fair value.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 84.70 voting (close of 9 November 2026, from equitylk.lk); non-voting about Rs 63.50 (same source, date not shown). Please check both live. In July–September 2026 the voting share traded between Rs 78.50 and Rs 99.90; in January–March 2026 between Rs 68.00 and Rs 117.50.
Six months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited): revenue Rs 36.78bn, up 27%. Gross margin fell to 29.6% from 31.8%. Finance costs rose 25% to Rs 870mn. Profit to shareholders Rs 1.50bn, down 10%; EPS Rs 3.41 (Rs 3.79). The September quarter alone: revenue up 28%, EPS Rs 1.96 (Rs 2.27).
Year to March 2026 (audited): revenue Rs 61.01bn (up 22%), profit Rs 2.57bn (down 25%), EPS Rs 5.83 (Rs 7.83), ROE 8.1%, dividend Rs 2.50. Sales volume 1.82 Mn MT, up 28% against industry growth of 19%. The chairman says local makers chose to absorb rising costs rather than raise prices.
Debt: borrowings and overdrafts Rs 16.87bn and cash Rs 2.08bn at September 2026, so net debt about Rs 14.8bn, 0.46x equity (Rs 10.1bn a year earlier in March 2025). Interest cover fell to 3.4x in 2025/26 from 5.6x.
Cash: operating cash flow was only Rs 1.40bn in 2025/26 (inventory rose Rs 3.2bn) against Rs 4.81bn of capital spending, so loans paid for the expansion and the dividend. In the six months to September 2026 operating cash was Rs 1.27bn and capital spending fell to Rs 0.49bn.
Industry: local capacity is about 10.7 Mn MT a year against demand of about 5.3 Mn MT in 2025, so the market is oversupplied and price-sensitive.

Record (years to March): EPS Rs -0.94 (2022), 11.31, 5.48, 7.83, 5.83 (2026). ROE -1.8%, 19.3%, 8.8%, 11.5%, 8.1%; 24.7% in 2021. Dividends Rs 0, 1.50, 2.00, 2.25, 2.50.

Methods
NAV (Rs 72.51): voting 1.17x, non-voting about 0.88x.
Return on equity: 8.1% last year, about 7.6% on the last twelve months, 9.2% average over five years. Below the cost of equity, so each rupee kept in the business is worth less than a rupee to shareholders.
P/E: 15.5x trailing EPS of Rs 5.45 (voting); about 11.7x for the non-voting share. Year-end P/E 15.3x (2026), 10.1x (2025).
Dividends: Rs 2.50 for 2025/26, a 3.0% yield (3.9% on the non-voting share), 43% of profit. A dividend model gives only Rs 19 / 27 / 41 and is shown as a check, not used in fair value.
Justified price to book: Rs 18.1 / 42.0 / 82.9, weighted Rs 43.0.
P/E method: Rs 39.2 / 57.0 / 79.2, weighted Rs 56.1.
Residual income: Rs 18.9 / 34.4 / 65.0, weighted Rs 35.9.
Scenario averages: Rs 25.4 / 44.4 / 75.7. Weighted 30/50/20: fair value about Rs 45.0 (0.62x NAV). Buy price (15% below) Rs 38.30; strong buy (25% below) Rs 33.80.

Assumptions (bear / base / bull)
Cost of equity: 17% / 15.5% / 14% (bonds about 12% plus a premium; Tokyo is the market leader with moderate debt).
Long-run ROE: 8% / 11.5% / 15% (five-year average about 9%, six-year average about 11.7%).
Long-term growth: 5% / 6% / 7%.
EPS for the year to March 2027 × P/E: Rs 4.90 × 8 / Rs 5.70 × 10 / Rs 6.60 × 12 (first half Rs 3.41; second half of last year Rs 2.04).
Residual income starts from today's ROE of about 7.6% and moves to the long-run ROE over ten years, paying out 43%.

What would change the view
Higher: cement price increases that restore gross margin above 33%; ROE back above 13% for two years; borrowings falling now the big projects are done; a construction boom (port, housing, reconstruction after Cyclone Ditwah).
Lower: a price war with importers and other local makers in an oversupplied market; rupee weakness and fuel costs; higher interest rates on Rs 13.6bn of short-term loans; another round of large capital spending.

Buy plan for 500 shares
200 at up to Rs 45.00, 150 at up to Rs 38.30, 150 at up to Rs 33.80: about Rs 19,800 in total (average Rs 39.63), against Rs 42,350 at today's voting price or about Rs 31,750 for non-voting shares. Rs 45 is about 47% below today's voting price. The voting share was Rs 42 at its low in January–March 2025 and closed at Rs 33.90 in March 2022, so it has been there in bad years, but it isn't likely soon. The non-voting share needs about a 29% fall to reach Rs 45; it was Rs 37.50 at its low in January–March 2025.

Business tests (1 of 4 passed: weak, category 3 'avoid for now')
Return on equity of 15% or more: fail (8.1%; five-year average about 9%).
Net debt no more than equity: pass (0.46x).
Steady profit: fail (loss in 2021/22; profit down 25% last year and 10% in the latest half).
Profit turns into cash: fail (2025/26 operating cash Rs 1.40bn against profit Rs 2.57bn; expansion and dividend paid with loans). Borderline: 2024/25 and the latest half were better.

Risks and caveats: the three interim reports are scanned images read by text recognition; check any figure that matters. The voting price is from a third-party site; the site replaces it with the daily CSE close. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.
